Subject: Onboarding: Benchmark plan and acceptance criteria for HelixPay

Hi Susan and HelixPay Ops team,

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. As discussed, attached is our first-pass load test plan (hlx_load_plan_v1.xlsx) and a short mutual-action summary so engineering and your QA can validate expectations. High-level acceptance criteria we agreed:

- Steady-state throughput: 250 req/s sustained for 30 minutes (95th percentile latency target applies)
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile <= 220 ms token-generation tail (end-to-end request to final token)
- Tail latency: 99th percentile <= 520 ms (for traffic spikes simulated in window W3)
- Error rate: <0.5% (5xx or timeout) during load windows
- Cold-start/scale-up ramp: recover to 80% target throughput within 90s of simulated service restart

Key test windows in the plan:
W1: functional smoke (low concurrency)
W2: steady-state ramp to 250 req/s (verify batching & KV cache hit rates)
W3: burst/spike (simulate 2x for 10 minutes)
W4: resilience (node restart + degraded model variant fallback)

Operational notes: we recommend enabling prefix caching for repeated prompt families during W2 to reduce per-token cost; Karthik flagged a quantization profile that keeps FP16 for attention kernels (we'll test both q4 and q8-lite). Monica will run the telemetry capture to record per-route token counts, batching stats, and kv-cache hit rates.

Please confirm HelixPay's preferred test windows (UTC offsets in the sheet) and any additional constraints (e.g., maintenance blackout between 06:00-10:00 UTC). We'll reserve a Dedicated pool for the W2/W3 windows you confirm.

Attachments: hlx_load_plan_v1.xlsx (xlsx, ~28KB); redwood_inference_mutual_action_plan.pdf (pdf, ~12KB)

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan

Great questions, Susan — answers inline below.

1) Request definition: For the acceptance criteria above, a "request" = one model inference call (single RPC). If your simulation uses multi-turn user flows that generate 1.8 calls on average per session, please scale the session traffic accordingly; we've included a small helper in the spreadsheet (sheet: traffic-mapping) to convert sessions -> calls. Batching behavior will be measured per RPC; we will report average batch size and per-token latency.

2) W3 timing: 2027-06-22 02:00-06:00 UTC works for us. We'll schedule the Dedicated pool and reserve 2 extra burst slots. Monica, please confirm reserved capacity and telemetry window.

3) Telemetry bundle: attached is a sample schema (also in the Drive link). We'll deliver a CSV and JSON telemetry bundle that includes: timestamp, route, request_id, model_variant, batch_size, tokens_in, tokens_out, kv_cache_hit (true/false), server_p95_latency_ms, server_p99_latency_ms, error_code. HelixPay's ops can map request_id -> internal session id.

Fallback model: Redwood will provide the smaller quantized variant for W4 and can pre-warm it if you want — but our recommendation is to validate both options: (A) Redwood-managed fallback (auto fallback to quantized variant on errors) and (B) HelixPay-managed warm standby. We'll include both in the run matrix; choose which you prefer for the final acceptance signoff.

Action items:
- HelixPay Ops: confirm W2/W3 windows and whether session-level or RPC-level traffic will be simulated (susan + ops+qa)
- Monica: confirm dedicated capacity reservation and telemetry capture plan
- Karthik: prepare the q4 / q8-lite perf comparison and a short note on expected tokenization differences

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the W2 ramp and a short pre-run checklist.

Thanks,
Priya
